> A question: if a pod is deleted between assumed and bound to a node, scheduler will try to forget it calling `sched.SchedulerCache.ForgetPod(assumed)`, e.g. if scheduler fails to bind a pod because it is deleted, it will try to forget it at
>

>

Thanks. I think we should not return err or return `NotFound` if pod have been removed from assumed pods in `ForgetPod` func.
I would modify This PR.

> BTW: snapshot info is not intended for use at bind cycle.

Actually, we have cached the pods to be scheduled locally. 
Snapshot is mainly used for calculating the remaining resources when `Filter`. However, if duplicated pods exist, the resource cached by the snapshot may be incorrect?

> If it has been forgotten, it seems that there is no need to remove it again?

Sorry for misunderstanding, I mean if we have called `sched.SchedulerCache.ForgetPod(assumed)`, need we call `sched.SchedulerCache.RemoveAssumedPod(pod)` to remove the assumed pod again?

> However, if duplicated pods exist, the resource cached by the snapshot may be incorrect?

The two pods have different pod UID, so from scheduler's perspective, they are different pods. Snapshot is updated at each schedule cycle. How long does the duplicated pods exist in snapshot info?

I agree with @hex108. 

I think we have the following cases:

1) If the binding succeeded before the pod got deleted, then the pod will have NodeName set (i.e., the pod is assigned), and the scheduler will then get an add then a delete event that will be handled by the [delete event handler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L362), which will remove the pod from the cache.

2) If for some reason the scheduler didn't receive the add and delete events in the right order, then it seems that the pod will not be removed from the scheduler cache immediately, but it will eventually expire and get removed at most after 30 sec after the binding finished (whether it succeeded or not).

3) If the pod got deleted before binding is finished, then the binding should fail and the scheduler will call [ForgetPod](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L575), which will remove the pod from the cache.



Remember that the system by design is eventually consistent, and plugins should be designed with that in mind, so I don't see that this is something we necessarily need to address.

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/21016#discussion_r52728635

Assumed pods would not be removed when pods have deleted immediately.
Normally, it would not influence the scheduling progress.However since Framework  Handler provides GetShapshot() func, users may use snapShot to implement their own scheduler. e.g. we implemented  gang-scheduling which relies on the snapshot.

I have sent a PR to fix it.

Just to clarify, those are not duplicate pods, they are two different pods (pods with different UID) with the same name.

To summarize the issue: when an assumed pod gets deleted, the scheduler does not seem to remove it immediately from its cache, rather it just waits until the pod expires on its own (maximum 30 second). This behavior is not new, and the history behind it is not clear to me.

Copying a comment I made on the PR:


I think we have the following cases:

1) If the binding succeeded before the pod got deleted, then the pod will have NodeName set (i.e., the pod is assigned), and the scheduler will then get an add then a delete event that will be handled by the [delete event handler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L362), which will remove the pod from the cache.

2) If for some reason the scheduler didn't receive the add and delete events in the right order, then it seems that the pod will not be removed from the scheduler cache immediately, but it will eventually expire and get removed at most after 30 sec after the binding finished.

3) If the pod got deleted before the binding is finished, then the binding should fail and the scheduler will call [ForgetPod](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L575), which will remove the pod from the cache.



Remember that the system by design is eventually consistent, and plugins should be designed with that in mind, so I don't see that this is something we necessarily need to address.

Seems the issue I met does match the cases you mentioned.

From the codes, if the pod is deleted before binding is finished, but pod is assumed.
Then a delete event comes, scheduler will not call` ForgetPod`, it will call https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L386, because the pod has not been scheduled, then the pod would not be removed from the cache, so the pod exists in the cache util expires.

ForgetPod will be called [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L575) if the binding failed, and this will happen if the delete on the apiserver was performed before the bind was successful.

I think the case you are hitting is that the binding was successful, but the delete happened right after, and the scheduler received a delete event before an add event (i.e., [case 2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/85563#issuecomment-559222479) above).

If that is indeed the case, then we could call ForgetPod in RemovePod if the pod is assumed.
@cwdsuzhou do you have a test that reproduces this case consistently?

> ForgetPod will be called [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L575) if the binding failed, and this will happen if the delete on the apiserver was performed before the bind was successful.
> 
> I think the case you are hitting is that the binding was successful, but the delete happened right after, and the scheduler received a delete event before an add event (i.e., [case 2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/85563#issuecomment-559222479) above).
> 
> If that is indeed the case, then we could call ForgetPod in RemovePod if the pod is assumed.

We are developing a gang-scheduler, so we would not permit the pods util descried number of pods reached, then the pods can not be bound. When we delete the pods , a delete event would receive, but due to not assign(binding), we would not call `ForgetPod`.

So I think do not match `case 2` you mentioned.

If some of the pods are waiting. Then we delete them and re-create them, the case I mentioned may happen.
so a delete is issued while the pod is waiting on permit? if so, who is doing that? the plugin you are developing? shouldn't you reject the pod first?

Thanks. 

Our plugin is based on 1.16, seems that we can not know if a pod has been deleted within the Plugin Framework.

However, I find in the latest version, when a pod is deleted, pod would be rejected since this PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84578 merged.
So, the issue may have fixed.
